text.title: Activation Framework Worked Example
text.summary: One complete activation spec for a B2B SaaS whose signups arrive but week-1 retention is weak: `project_created` within 7 days validated against D30 retention, a four-week closed-cohort baseline at 22 percent, a five-step funnel with one uninstrumented step, drop-offs ranked by users lost, two ICE-scored experiments and the weekly dashboard, with a note on each non-obvious value; then the spec as it is usually written and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Signups run at about 1,800 a week; D30 retention is 19 percent. The team calls a user "activated" when they "see value". The event table holds `signup_completed`, `email_verified`, `workspace_named`, `project_created` and `acquisition_channel`; the onboarding modal's template choice emits nothing. Data cutoff for the spec is 2026-05-04.

example.title: project_created within 7 days
example.note: `project_created` within 7 days replaced "sees value" because it is a row in the event table and a window makes it a query (r-single-activation-event-with-window). The March 2 cohort was chosen for the D30 comparison because signup plus 30 days is well before the cutoff; 46 percent versus 11 percent with 412 and 1,388 users is a gap a reviewer can trust, and the correlational note stays because forcing the event does not create retention (r-event-validated-against-d30-retention). The baseline stops at the week of April 20: its last signup day, April 26, plus 7 days is May 3, the day before the cutoff; the week of April 27 is open and left out (r-baseline-before-experiments). Each `activation_rate` is `activated` / `signups` to three decimals, and the funnel's first `entered` (7,145) and last `completed` (1,599) are the cohort totals. "template picked" has no event, so it carries a ticket and no figures; its drop is not reported anywhere (r-funnel-steps-map-to-events). "project created" ranks first with 3,304 users lost although "email verified" has the larger step count; ranking by `relative_drop` would give the same order here, but the rule is absolute loss and the validator recomputes it from `entered` - `completed` (r-dropoffs-ranked-by-absolute-loss). `ice` 7.67 is `round((8 + 7 + 8) / 3, 2)` from `templates/ice.py`, 7.0 is `(7 + 8 + 6) / 3`, and the list is sorted by it (r-ice-integer-scale-and-formula). The first experiment's `baseline_value` 0.224 is the pooled baseline rate (1,599 / 7,145); the second's 0.73 is the email step's conversion (5,216 / 7,145), because its metric is the step (r-experiment-names-step-metric-threshold). The dashboard repeats `window_days: 7` and its `series_id` encodes event and window, so switching to 14 days starts `-14d-v1` instead of rewriting history (r-dashboard-reports-closed-cohorts-weekly).

example.title: the same team's spec as usually written
example.note: What the validator prints: `activation_event.name` is a phrase with "or", not an event name (r-single-activation-event-with-window); only 2 baseline cohorts where 4 are required (r-baseline-before-experiments); the uninstrumented "template picked" step carries `entered` and `completed` (r-funnel-steps-map-to-events); `impact` 7.5 is not an integer and `confidence` 12 is above 10 (r-ice-integer-scale-and-formula); `dashboard.closed_cohorts_only` is false and `segment_by` lacks `acquisition_channel` (r-dashboard-reports-closed-cohorts-weekly). Once those are fixed the cross-field checks add: the performed group's D30 retention (0.11) is not above the other group's (0.11), so the event predicts nothing (convenient-event-not-predictive); the week of April 27 plus 7 days runs past the May 4 cutoff, which is the open cohort whose 17 percent looks like a regression (open-cohort-in-baseline); `dropoff_priorities` puts 600 users lost above 1,139 (percentage-only-ranking); and `dashboard.window_days` 14 disagrees with the event's 7. What the reviewer sees: a hypothesis with no mechanism and a backlog of one item that could not be re-scored by anyone else (ice-scores-unreproducible).
